rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إذ is syntactically governed by بغى عليهم, but it marks the narrative setting rather than the time of the transgression; some exegetes attach it to an implicit أذكر.
rows.anchor: ظرف منصوب بفعل ( بغى عليهم ) والمقصود من هذا الظرف القصة وليس القصد به توقيت البغي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: قومه can mean a group of Qarun’s people, namely those who admonished him.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالقوم بعضهم إما جماعة منهم وهم أهل الموعظة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it can refer to Moses, called the people because his words set an example for them, as though they had spoken them.
rows.anchor: وإما موسى عليه السلام أطلق عليه اسم القوم لأن أقواله قدوة للقوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Farah can mean joy, as in Yunus 10:22, or excessive elation, arrogance, and conceit, as in the usage at 13:26.
rows.anchor: والفرح يطلق على السرور كما في قوله تعالى { وفرحوا بها } في يونس ( 22 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibited joy is excessive attachment to worldly pleasures that turns one from good works, competition in virtue, spiritual perfection, and religious manners; 28:77 makes this contextual sense explicit.
rows.anchor: والفرح المنهي عنه هو المفرط منه ، أي الذي تمحض للتعلق بمتاع الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unqualified joy suggests a settled disposition of conceit and arrogance; the intensive form and causal clause condemn extreme absorption in pleasure, which entails neglect of serious duties.
rows.anchor: وأحسب أن الفرح إذا لم يعلق به شيء دل على أنه صار سجية الموصوف فصار مرادا به العجب والبطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intensive form in لا يحب الفرحين means those excessive in joy; its causal force makes the prohibition a warning against turning from serious obligations.
rows.anchor: وقد أشير إلى بيان المقصود تعضيدا لدلالة المقام بقوله { إن الله لا يحب الفرحين } ، أي المفرطين في الفرح فإن صيغة ( فعل ) صيغة مبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking the afterlife means seeking its bliss and reward.
rows.anchor: وابتغاء الدار الآخرة طلبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ظرفية in فيما آتاك الله is figurative: Qarun should use the greater part of God’s gifts, his treasure, to seek the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وعلق بفعل الابتغاء قوله { فيما ءاتاك الله } بحرف الظرفية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The figurative sense is like رزقوهم فيها واكسوهم in 4:5, meaning give them from it and from its greater portion.
rows.anchor: فالظرفية هنا كالتي في قوله تعالى { وارزقوهم فيها واكسوهم } ( النساء : 5 ) أي منها ومعظمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poetic example supports figurative ظرفية: seek reward by spending Qarun’s treasures in God’s way and in the required and encouraged acts of charity.
rows.anchor: ونشرب في أثمانها ونقامر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarun is urged to gain reward by giving from his treasures for God’s cause, obligatory duties, and recommended charitable works.
rows.anchor: أي اطلب بكنوزك أسباب حصول الثواب بالإنفاق منها في سبيل الله وما أوجبه ورغب فيه من القربان ووجوه البر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence is parenthetical between the two surrounding clauses, and its waw is parenthetical.
rows.anchor: جملة معترضة بين الجملتين الحافتين بها ، والواو اعتراضية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition is permissive, and forgetfulness figuratively means neglect: Qarun may take a worldly share that does not consume his share of the afterlife.
rows.anchor: والنهي في { ولا تنس نصيبك } مستعمل في الإباحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This qualification softens the admonition so Qarun will not infer that he must devote all his wealth to worship and reject every worldly pleasure; he may enjoy some of it after paying God’s due.
rows.anchor: وهذا احتراس في الموعظة خشية نفور الموعوظ من موعظة الواعظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naṣīb means a share or portion; the word derives from نصب because what is allotted to someone is set out and distinguished.
rows.anchor: والنصيب : الحظ والقسط ، وهو فعيل من النصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The possessive نصيبك marks a personal right to use wealth for fitting worldly enjoyment, provided it is neither worship nor forbidden.
rows.anchor: وإضافة النصيب إلى ضميره دالة على أنه حقه وأن للمرء الانتفاع بماله في ما يلائمه في الدنيا خاصة مما ليس من القربات ولم يكن حراما

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik says the worldly share means living, eating, and drinking without undue restriction.
rows.anchor: قال مالك : في رأيي معنى { ولا تنس نصيبك من الدنيا }

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the worldly share is everything lawful.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة : نصيب الدنيا هو الحلال كله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse exemplifies a prohibitive form used to convey permission; من is partitive, and الدنيا means worldly enjoyment, of which the person has a share.
rows.anchor: وبذلك تكون هذه الآية مثالا لاستعمال صيغة النهي لمعنى الإباحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Beneficence already falls under seeking the afterlife, but it is singled out to prepare the argument based on God’s beneficence to Qarun.
rows.anchor: الإحسان داخل في عموم ابتغاء الدار الآخرة ولكنه ذكر هنا ليبنى عليه الاحتجاج بقوله { كما أحسن الله إليك }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The kāf marks comparison and ما is a verbal noun: render beneficence like God’s beneficence; its causal force arises from comparison rather than being a separate meaning of kāf.
rows.anchor: والكاف للتشبيه ، و ( ما ) مصدرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The likeness is that gratitude for each blessing should take a corresponding form; grammarians call the kāf causal, as in 2:198, but causality follows from comparison.
rows.anchor: والتحقيق أن التعليل حاصل من معنى التشبيه وليس معنى مستقلا من معاني الكاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of أحسن is omitted to generalize beneficence toward oneself, one’s people, animals, and other creatures within one’s power to help.
rows.anchor: وحذف متعلق الإحسان لتعميم ما يحسن إليه فيشمل نفسه وقومه ودوابه ومخلوقات الله الداخلة في دائرة التمكن من الإحسان إليها

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A hadith says God prescribed excellence in every thing; the author gives no grading.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : ( إن الله كتب الإحسان على كل شيء )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Beneficence suits each recipient and situation, including keeping permitted harm to its measure and showing good speech, a welcoming face, and a pleasant manner.
rows.anchor: فالإحسان في كل شيء بحسبه ، والإحسان لكل شيء بما يناسبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition is added because doing good to some while harming others might be mistaken for overall beneficence; the explicit warning bars mixing good with corruption.
rows.anchor: وعطف { لا تبغ الفساد في الأرض } للتحذير من خلط الإحسان بالفساد فإن الفساد ضد الإحسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth means the land where Qarun’s people live; since it is part of the globe, corruption there is corruption within the earth as a whole.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالأرض أرضهم التي هم حالون بها ، وإذ قد كانت جزءا من الكرة الأرضية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording has parallels including 2:205, where someone turns away and strives to corrupt the earth.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدمت نظائره منها في قوله تعالى { وإذا تولى سعى في الأرض ليفسد فيها } في سورة البقرة ( 205 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s lack of love for corrupters explains the prohibition: servants may not do what God does not love.
rows.anchor: وجملة { إن الله لا يحب المفسدين } علة للنهي عن الإفساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarun was a monotheist following Israel’s religion, but doubted Moses’ promises and prescriptions.
rows.anchor: وقد كان { قارون } موحدا على دين إسرائيل ولكنه كان شاكا في صدق مواعيد موسى وفي تشريعاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarun’s unconnected reply is a self-important answer meant to silence his admonishers after their rebuke challenged his pride.
rows.anchor: جواب عن موعظة واعظيه من قومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إنما combines إن with the blocking ما as one particle; its correct spelling joins the nūn to mīm, and it restricts the claim to one cause.
rows.anchor: و { إنما } هذه هي أداة الحصر المركبة من ( إن ) و ( ما ) الكافة مصيرتين كلمة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarun claims that he was given the wealth solely because of knowledge he possesses.
rows.anchor: والمعنى : ما أوتيت هذا المال إلا على علم علمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in أوتيته refers to the relative ما in the admonishers’ earlier phrase فيما آتاك الله; the passive voice leaves the giver understood from their words.
rows.anchor: وضمير { أوتيته } عائد إلى ( ما ) الموصولة في قولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: على علم is circumstantial, qualifying the nominative pronoun in the passive verb.
rows.anchor: و { على علم } في موضع الحال من الضمير المرفوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عندي qualifies علم, emphasizing Qarun’s command of the knowledge and his reputation for it; this reading best fits the following rebuke.
rows.anchor: وقوله { عندي } صفة ل { علم } تأكيدا لتمكنه من العلم وشهرته به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers this construction because it coheres with the ensuing reminder that God destroyed earlier generations.
rows.anchor: هذا هو الوجه في تفسير هذه الجملة من الآية وهو الذي يستقيم مع قوله تعالى عقبه { أو لم يعلم أن الله قد أهلك من قبله من القرون } الآية

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Other commentators propose different constructions for على, العلم, and عندي, but the author does not detail them.
rows.anchor: وذكر المفسرون وجوها تسفر عن أشكال أخرى من تركيب نظم الآية في محمل معنى { على } ومحمل المراد من ( العلم ) ومحمل { عندي }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discourse now turns to address the Muslims.
rows.anchor: وقوله { أو لم يعلم } الآية إقبال على خطاب المسلمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative hamza expresses emphatic rebuke and astonishment that Qarun failed to heed God’s destruction of people who exulted in blessings and strength, as though he had forgotten what he knew.
rows.anchor: والهمزة في { أو لم يعلم } للاستفهام الإنكاري التعجيبي تعجيبا من عدم جريه على موجب علمه بأن الله أهلك أمما على بطرهم النعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surprise is that Qarun remembered much knowledge yet let this lesson slip, as the proverb says, one remembered something while forgetting other things.
rows.anchor: ونسيانه حتى صار كأنه لم يعلمه تعجيبا من فوات مراعاة ذلك منه مع سعة علمه بغيره من باب ( حفظت شيئا وغابت عنك أشياء )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative clause is parenthetical between parts of the story, attached to Qarun’s claim.
rows.anchor: وعطف هذا الاستفهام على جملة { قال إنما أوتيته }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Strength is what enables difficult tasks, by analogy with bodily power for carrying heavy loads; compare 8:60.
rows.anchor: والقوة : ما به يستعان على الأعمال الصعبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: جمع means a gathered group of people.
rows.anchor: والجمع : الجماعة من الناس

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An unnamed view says Qarun’s followers numbered 250 Israelite leaders over groups.
rows.anchor: قيل : كان أشياع قارون مائتين وخمسين من بني إسرائيل رؤساء جماعات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing sentence is an independent summary, not coordinated with God’s destruction of earlier generations.
rows.anchor: وجملة { ولا يسأل عن ذنوبهم المجرمون } تذييل للكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denied questioning is in this world, not the questioning of the afterlife.
rows.anchor: والسؤال المنفي السؤال في الدنيا وليس سؤال الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possibility is that questioning figuratively denies any need to inquire: God knows their sins and punishes their crimes; the warning tells criminals to fear sudden seizure.
rows.anchor: والمعنى : يحتمل أن يكون السؤال كناية عن عدم الحاجة إلى السؤال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the question is literal: a criminal is not questioned before punishment because the messengers clarified good and evil and God gave respite; then He may seize them suddenly, as at 6:44.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون السؤال بمعناه الحقيقي ، أي لا يسأل المجرم عن جرمه قبل عقابه

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet is quoted as saying God gives an unjust person respite, then seizes him without letting him escape; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: وقول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ( إن الله يمهل الظالم حتى إذا أخذه لم يفلته )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The waw may coordinate this statement with the learned people’s speech, commanding those tempted by Qarun’s state to patiently bear their deprivation.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن تكون الواو للعطف فهي من كلام { الذين أوتوا العلم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the waw is parenthetical, and God interjects to teach His servants the virtue of patience; the author gives both analyses without preference.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون الواو اعتراضية والجملة معترضة من جانب الله تعالى علم بها عباده فضيلة الصبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine pronoun may refer to the quality of God’s reward.
rows.anchor: وضمير { يلقاها } عائد إلى مفهوم من الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it refers to the upright way, the way of faith and good works.
rows.anchor: أو السيرة القويمة ، وهي سيرة الإيمان والعمل الصالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Talqiya literally makes something meet another; here it is metaphorical for giving a great quality or way, attained only by the patient.
rows.anchor: والتلقية : جعل الشيء لاقيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Patience enables people to attain great aims through the hardships and obstacles of striving; without it, resolve weakens and they abandon the aim.
rows.anchor: لأن الصبر وسيلة لنوال الأمور العظيمة لاحتياج السعي لها إلى تجلد لما يعرض في خلاله من مصاعب وعقبات كأداء فإن لم يكن المرء متخلقا بالصبر خارت عزيمته فترك ذاك لذاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ف marks the punishment’s immediate sequence after Qarun’s proud display, the crowd’s wish to resemble him, and the scholars’ correction, while those wishful onlookers saw his punishment.
rows.anchor: دلت الفاء على تعقيب ساعة خروج قارون في ازدهائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khasf is the turning of the earth’s surface into its interior, or the reverse; the subsidence occurs through earthquake force, while eclipsing the sun is a figurative use.
rows.anchor: والخسف : انقلاب بعض ظاهر الأرض إلى باطنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ means accompaniment: God made the earth sink together with Qarun and his house.
rows.anchor: والباء في قوله { فخسفنا به } باء المصاحبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This extraordinary subsidence affected Qarun and those immediately with him, not the wider area, and was a miracle for Moses.
rows.anchor: وهذا الخسف خارق للعادة لأنه لم يتناول غير قارون ومن ظاهره

rows.speaker: سفر العدد
rows.claim: Numbers 16 recounts Korah’s opposition to Moses, Moses’ warning and call for people to leave their tents, the earth swallowing Korah’s group and property alive, and fire destroying 250 men.
rows.anchor: جاء في الإصحاح السادس عشر من سفر العدد أن قورح ( وهو قارون ) ومن معه لما آذوا موسى كما تقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarun relied on many chiefs among the Levites and others who backed his challenge to Moses; the earth swallowed them with him, so none could help him.
rows.anchor: وقد كان قارون معتزا على موسى بالطائفة التي كانت شايعته على موسى

words: فما كان له من فئة ينصرونه من دون الله
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The faction he had prepared to support him against Moses perished with him, so he had no helper apart from God.
rows.anchor: فلذلك قال الله تعالى { فما كان له من فئة ينصرونه من دون الله }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: انتصر means to obtain victory: Qarun’s allies did not rescue him, and he could not save himself.
rows.anchor: يقال : انتصر فلان ، إذا حصل له النصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gave Abraham two rewards: worldly victory over enemies, good reputation, spreading monotheism, and abundant descendants; and the afterlife reward of joining the righteous.
rows.anchor: جمع الله له أجرين : أجرا في الدنيا بنصره على أعدائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite form indicates completeness: Abraham belongs among the fully righteous.
rows.anchor: وأجرا في الآخرة وهو كونه في زمرة الصالحين ، والتعريف للكمال ، أي من كمل الصالحين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The narrative moves from Abraham’s mission to Lot’s because Lot resembles Abraham in being saved by God from a punishment of torment.
rows.anchor: شابه إبراهيم في أن أنجاه الله من عذاب الرجز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening of this passage follows the pattern of 29:16 and has parallels in Sūrat al-Naml and Sūrat al-Shuʿarāʾ.
rows.anchor: الآية كالقول في آية { وإبراهيم إذ قال لقومه } ( العنكبوت : 16 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Variations among the repeated accounts are narrative variety serving the purpose stated in the seventh introduction; this declaration about the indecency is unique to this telling.
rows.anchor: وما بين الآيات من تفاوت هو تفنن في حكاية القصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lot’s people were Canaanites, previously mentioned in Sūrat al-Aʿrāf.
rows.anchor: وقوم لوط من الكنعانيين وتقدم ذكرهم في سورة الأعراف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The إن and lām focus affirmation on the object of the predication, not merely on the proposition: what they do is a grave indecency.
rows.anchor: وتوكيد الجملة ب ( إن ) واللام توكيد لتعلق النسبة بالمفعول لا تأكيد للنسبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fāḥishah is an act at the extreme limit of ugliness; the emphasis confronts people who were not aware of their act’s shamefulness.
rows.anchor: فالمقصود تحقيق أن الذي يفعلونه فاحشة

rows.speaker: نافع وابن كثير وابن عامر وحفص عن عاصم وأبو جعفر
rows.claim: These readers pronounce the phrase with one hamza as a declarative used for rebuke.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن كثير وابن عامر وحفص عن عاصم وأبو جعفر { إنكم لتأتون الفاحشة } بهمزة واحدة على الإخبار المستعمل في التوبيخ

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي وأبو بكر عن عاصم ويعقوب وخلف
rows.claim: These readers pronounce it with two hamzas, an interrogative hamza followed by إن.
rows.anchor: وقرأه أبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي وأبو بكر عن عاصم

rows.speaker: جميع القراء
rows.claim: All readers pronounce the corresponding question about approaching men with two hamzas.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجميع { أإنكم لتأتون الرجال } بهمزتين

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf reports Abu Ubayd’s observation that the first phrase is written with one letter, whereas the second phrase has yāʾ and nūn; perhaps the codex is Basran or Kufan, making its readers’ transmission differ from the written form.
rows.anchor: وفي ( الكشاف ) : قال أبو عبيد : وجدت الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question about approaching men and the coordinated actions is an appositional expansion of the general charge of indecency; the further offenses are included in that charge.
rows.anchor: وجملة { أينكم لتأتون الرجال } الخ بدل اشتمال من مضمون جملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denunciatory question covers the entire list and repeats the emphatic particle so the appositional clause matches its antecedent.
rows.anchor: وأدخل استفهام الإنكار على جميع التفصيل وأعيد حرف التأكيد لتتطابق جملة البدل مع الجملة المبدل منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cutting the road means attacking travelers by taking property, killing them, or coercing them into indecency.
rows.anchor: وقطع السبيل : قطع الطريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lot’s people used to sit along the roads to seize whichever passersby they chose.
rows.anchor: وكان قوم لوط يقعدون بالطرق ليأخذوا من المارة من يختارونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Road attacks are inherently corrupt and especially corrupt in this aim.
rows.anchor: فقطع السبيل فساد في ذاته وهو أفسد في هذا المقصد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They used their gathering to discuss, prepare for, and initiate the indecency, including flirtation and casting pebbles to choose a target; public display worsened it by abandoning concealment and spreading the practice.
rows.anchor: وأما إتيان المنكر في ناديهم فإنهم جعلوا ناديهم للحديث في ذكر هذه الفاحشة والاستعداد لها ومقدماتها كالتغازل برمي الحصى اقتراعا بينهم على من يرومونه

words: ما سبقكم بها من أحد من العالمين
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase intensifies blame: they introduced this vile practice, which had not occurred to anyone; witnessing a novel vice can awaken desire and normalize it.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله { ما سبقكم بها من أحد من العالمين } تشديد في الإنكار عليهم في أنهم الذين سنوا هذه الفاحشة السيئة للناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A nādī is the daytime place of gathering, conversation, and consultation, from nadw, assembly by day; a nighttime gathering is a sāmir, and an empty meeting place is not called a nādī.
rows.anchor: والنادي : المكان الذي ينتدي فيه الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The term applies to the meeting place only while its people are present; after they leave, it is no longer called a nādī.
rows.anchor: ولا يقال للمجلس ناد إلا ما دام فيه أهله فإذا قاموا عنه لم يسم ناديا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The response parallels 29:24, where Lot’s people answer by demanding his death; the command to bring punishment is a challenge and implies that he had warned them of punishment during his mission.
rows.anchor: الكلام فيه كالقول في نظيره المتقدم آنفا في قوله { فما كان جواب قومه إلا أن قالوا اقتلوه } ( العنكبوت : 24 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their command is meant to declare Lot powerless; it implies that he warned them of punishment, a normal part of prophetic preaching even though the earlier account omitted it.
rows.anchor: والأمر في { ائتنا بعذاب الله } للتعجيز وهو يقتضي أنه أنذرهم العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens and earth include both themselves and all beings contained within them; their precise creation demonstrates the Creator’s oneness and attributes.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالسماوات والأرض ما يشمل ذاتهما والموجودات المظروفة فيهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After presenting earlier peoples as an example, the passage clarifies the falsehood of the polytheists’ creed and praises believers’ sound belief, then addresses the Messenger to strengthen him in preaching and observance and benefit believers.
rows.anchor: بعد أن ضرب الله للناس المثل بالأمم السالفة جاء بالحجة المبينة فساد معتقد المشركين

words: اتل ما أوحي إليك من الكتاب
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command strengthens the Messenger in spreading the call, observing religious duties, and proclaiming God’s word; believers who benefited from proofs of unity share its benefit.
rows.anchor: أقبل على رسوله بالخطاب الذي يزيد تثبيته على نشر الدعوة وملازمة الشرائع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Messenger is the believers’ exemplar and leader, so the command extends to them, as confirmed by its plural ending and 11:112.
rows.anchor: وما الرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام إلا قدوة للمؤمنين وسيدهم فأمره أمر لهم كما دل عليه التذييل بقوله { والله يعلم ما تصنعون } بصيغة جمع المخاطبين كقوله { فاستقم كما أمرت ومن تاب معك } ( هود : 112 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of اتل is omitted so recitation includes addressing both Muslims and polytheists, as in 27:91–92.
rows.anchor: وحذف متعلق فعل { اتل } ليعم التلاوة على المسلمين وعلى المشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer is a great deed; this command also applies to the whole community, since establishing prayer is repeatedly commanded throughout the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: وأمره بإقامة الصلاة لأن الصلاة عمل عظيم ، وهذا الأمر يشمل الأمة

words: إِنَّ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ تَنْهَىٰ عَنِ ٱلْفَحْشَآءِ وَٱلْمُنكَرِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إن functions like a causal فاء here, explaining the command to establish prayer.
rows.anchor: وعلل الأمر بإقامة الصلاة بالإشارة إلى ما فيها من الصلاح النفساني

words: إِنَّ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ تَنْهَىٰ عَنِ ٱلْفَحْشَآءِ وَٱلْمُنكَرِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reasoning chiefly addresses the community, since the Prophet is protected from indecency; the verse explains prayer’s benefit but not the command to recite, because this benefit is a divine secret learned through revelation.
rows.anchor: ولا شك أن هذا التعليل موجه إلى الأمة لأن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم معصوم من الفحشاء والمنكر فاقتصر على تعليل الأمر بإقامة الصلاة دون تعليل الأمر بتلاوة القرآن لما في هذا الصلاح الذي جعله الله في الصلاة من سر إلهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Standing, bowing, and prostration express humility before God and remind worshippers to seek His pleasure and avoid His anger, deterring indecency and wrong.
rows.anchor: وفي الصلاة أفعال هي خضوع وتذلل لله تعالى من قيام وركوع وسجود وذلك يذكر بلزوم اجتلاب مرضاته والتباعد عن سخطه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer’s inward acts of intention and readiness to stand before God remind worshippers to obey His commands and avoid His prohibitions.
rows.anchor: وفي الصلاة أعمال قلبية من نية واستعداد للوقوف بين يدي الله وذلك يذكر بأن المعبود جدير بأن تمتثل أوامره وتجتنب نواهيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Through its combined acts, prayer functions as an admonisher; saying it prohibits sin portrays moral counsel rather than forceful diversion or restraint.
rows.anchor: فكانت الصلاة بمجموعها كالواعظ الناهي عن الفحشاء والمنكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People vary in response, and prayer is distributed through day and night to renew reminders; repetition strengthens piety until it becomes a settled trait, with a further divine property easing avoidance of sin.
rows.anchor: ثم الناس في الانتهاء متفاوتون

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that a man told the Prophet someone prayed at night but stole in the morning; the Prophet replied that the prayer would soon stop him. No grading is stated.
rows.anchor: روى أحمد وابن حبان والبيهقي عن أبي هريرة قال : ( جاء رجل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال : إن فلانا يصلي بالليل فإذا أصبح سرق ، فقال : سينهاه ما تقول ) أي صلاته بالليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article marks the generic classes; whenever prayer recalls God’s greatness, duty, and possible sins, it restrains the worshipper from some instances.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن التعريف في قوله { الفحشاء والمنكر } تعريف الجنس فكلما تذكر المصلي عند صلاته عظمة ربه ووجوب طاعته وذكر ما قد يفعله من الفحشاء والمنكر كانت صلاته حينئذ قد نهته عن بعض أفراد الفحشاء والمنكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faḥshāʾ denotes an act exceeding an accepted limit; here it means speech or action beyond what religious law permits, as in 2:169.
rows.anchor: و { الفحشاء } : اسم للفاحشة ، والفحش : تجاوز الحد المقبول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Munkar means whatever religious law rejects and does not approve.
rows.anchor: وبالمنكر : ما ينكره الشرع ولا يرضى بوقوعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two terms are paired because they express distinct grounds for condemnation and prohibition.
rows.anchor: وكأن الجمع بين الفاحشة والمنكر منظور فيه إلى اختلاف جهة ذمه والنهي عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause may coordinate with the claim that prayer prohibits wrongdoing; dhikr then means prayer, as in 62:9.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون عطفا على جملة { إن الصلاة تنهى عن الفحشاء والمنكر }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that reading, prayer prohibits wrongdoing because it is God’s remembrance; أكبر conveys intensity rather than comparison.
rows.anchor: أي إنما كانت ناهية عن الفحشاء والمنكر لأنها ذكر الله وذكر الله أمر كبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the clause coordinates with the command to recite, and ذكر الله means recalling God’s greatness; the superlative is noncomparative.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون عطفا على جملة { اتل ما أوحي إليك من الكتاب } . والمعنى : واذكر الله فإن ذكر الله أمر عظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, dhikr means verbal remembrance, in prayer and beyond; the sense resembles Muʿadh ibn Jabal’s statement that no human deed saves more from punishment than remembering God.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المراد ذكر الله باللسان ليعم ذكر الله في الصلاة وغيرها

rows.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
rows.claim: Muʿadh ibn Jabal says no deed a person performs is more saving from God’s punishment than remembrance of God.
rows.anchor: ويكون في معنى قول معاذ بن جبل ( ما عمل آدمي عملا أنجى له من عذاب الله من ذكر الله )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third reading takes dhikr as remembering God’s commands and prohibitions, vigilance and fear of His anger; here greater is genuinely comparative, since this remembrance can be repeated more often and restrains sin more than prayer.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المراد بالذكر تذكر ما أمر الله به ونهى عنه

rows.speaker: عمر رضي الله عنه
rows.claim: Umar says that remembering God when facing His commands and prohibitions is better than thanking Him with the tongue.
rows.anchor: قريبا من قول عمر رضي الله عنه : أفضل من شكر الله باللسان ذكر الله عند أمره ونهيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth reading is that remembrance means belief in God’s existence and oneness, the foundation underlying the two commanded good deeds; faith is the greater root.
rows.anchor: ذكر الله هو الإيمان بوجوده وبأنه واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This returns from the commanded acts to the chapter’s condemnation of shirk and glorification of monotheism, beginning from 29:42.
rows.anchor: وذلك من رد العجز على الصدر عاد به إلى تعظيم أمر التوحيد وتفظيع الشرك من قوله { إن الله يعلم ما تدعون من دونه من شيء } ( العنكبوت : 42 ) إلى هنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing clause summarizes the preceding commands and warning; it promises and threatens in light of recitation, prayer, and avoidance of wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: وقوله { والله يعلم ما تصنعون } تذييل لما قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: صنع means work or deed.
rows.anchor: والصنع : العمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command about disputation attaches to the recitation command in 29:45, since recitation entails leaving idolaters alone and refraining from debate after 29:43.
rows.anchor: عطف على جملة { اتل ما أوحي إليك من الكتاب } ( العنكبوت : 45 ) الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse prepares for post-Hijra debate with the People of the Book in Medina; Meccan Muslims had not encountered that situation, and the preceding polemic, including the spider parable, sets up the transition before the discussion with polytheists resumes at 29:47.
rows.anchor: وقد كانت هذه توطئة لما سيحدث من الدعوة في المدينة بعد هجرة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لأن مجادلة أهل الكتاب لا تعرض للنبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم ولا للمؤمنين في مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is parenthetical between the argument against polytheists and its resumption at 29:47, preparing a new mode of address.
rows.anchor: فهذه الآية معترضة بين محاجة المشركين والعود إليها في قوله تعالى { وكذلك أنزلنا إليك الكتاب } ( العنكبوت : 47 ) الآيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural prohibition includes the Prophet and Muslims, since believers might debate People of the Book when the Prophet was absent or before he arrived in Medina.
rows.anchor: وجيء في النهي بصيغة الجمع ليعم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم والمسلمين إذ قد تعرض للمسلمين مجادلات مع أهل الكتاب في غير حضرة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أو قبل قدومه المدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jidāl is disputation: presenting evidence for a position on which one disagrees with another; compare 4:107.
rows.anchor: والمجادلة : مفاعلة من الجدل ، وهو إقامة الدليل على رأي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This verse concerns debate, not fighting the People of the Book, so it should not be used to raise the question of whether a fighting command abrogated it; debate can occur in peace or war.
rows.anchor: وبهذا يعلم أن لا علاقة لهذه الآية بحكم قتال أهل الكتاب
